items.followUp: Differentiate between Bus Topology and Mesh Topology, and state two advantages of each.

rubric.why: The defining difference is that star computers connect to a central device, while ring computers form a loop.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the basic arrangements of star and ring topologies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the central hub or switch in star topology and the closed loop in ring topology.

rubric.why: Both are valid advantages of star topology.
rubric.description: Gives two advantages of star topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid advantages of star topology.

rubric.why: In a ring, each computer connects to its neighbours as part of a loop.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that each computer connects to two neighbouring computers and the connections form a closed loop.

rubric.why: These are valid advantages of ring topology.
rubric.description: Gives two advantages of ring topology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two valid advantages of ring topology.

modelAnswer: Star topology: Each computer is connected to a central hub or switch.
Two advantages of star topology are that it is easy to add or remove a computer and a fault in one computer usually does not affect the others.
Ring topology: Each computer is connected to two neighbouring computers, forming a closed loop.
Two advantages of ring topology are orderly data transmission and equal access for the computers on the network.

items.followUp: List the main steps used to solve a problem with a computer.

rubric.why: A solution begins by understanding the problem and identifying the information needed and the expected result.
rubric.description: Analyzes the problem and identifies its inputs and outputs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing problem analysis, including identifying inputs and expected outputs.

rubric.why: A solution is designed, implemented, and checked for errors.
rubric.description: Describes designing, implementing, and checking the solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the main steps, such as designing an algorithm or flowchart, writing the program, and testing and debugging it.

modelAnswer: First, analyze the problem and identify its inputs, processing requirements, and expected outputs.
Then design an algorithm or flowchart, write the program, and test and debug it.

items.followUp: Give two ways in which a flowchart helps while developing a program.

rubric.why: A flowchart shows a solution’s steps and logic in a visual form.
rubric.description: States that flowcharts visually represent a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a flowchart shows the steps or logic of a problem visually.

rubric.why: Flowcharts can help people communicate a solution and review it for errors before programming.
rubric.description: States another use of a flowchart in problem solving.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid use such as communicating the solution or identifying errors before coding.

modelAnswer: A flowchart presents the steps and logic of a solution visually, so the problem is easier to understand.
It helps communicate the solution and identify errors before coding the program.

items.followUp: State one advantage and one disadvantage of using an algorithm to solve a problem.

rubric.why: These are valid advantages of using an algorithm.
rubric.description: Gives an advantage of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid advantage, such as being clear and step-by-step, being independent of a programming language, or helping with coding and debugging.

rubric.why: Algorithms can be lengthy or time-consuming to prepare for large or complex problems.
rubric.description: Gives a disadvantage of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid disadvantage, such as an algorithm becoming lengthy or time-consuming for a large or complex problem.

modelAnswer: Advantage: An algorithm gives a clear, step-by-step solution and is independent of any particular programming language.
Disadvantage: An algorithm can become lengthy and time-consuming to write for a large or complex problem.

items.followUp: What is invalid test data? Give one example.

rubric.why: Valid test data must have a data type allowed by the program’s requirements.
rubric.description: States that valid test data has the required data type.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the data has the correct or required type.

rubric.why: Valid test data must fall within the permitted range or otherwise satisfy the program’s input requirements.
rubric.description: States that valid test data meets the program’s input requirements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the data is within the acceptable range or meets the program’s input requirements.

modelAnswer: Valid test data is input data that meets the program's requirements, including the required type and acceptable range.
